clue.text: Being very tired, he had to go by public transport

parts.note: to bus is to travel by bus, the commonest public transport
he had contracts to he'd, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An exhausted man has no car and must take the bus home.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's order puts the travel verb first, though the clue gives it last. 'Being' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone worn out after effort is said to be utterly exhausted, slang that originated in America.

clue.text: Biscuit type that gets Violet upset

parts.note: a brand is a type or make

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the flower is read bottom to top

parts.note: the pansy is a member of the violet family, Viola

explanation.surface: A particular biscuit makes a girl called Violet cross.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet looks like a girl's name; it is the flower family, giving a pansy.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a thin, crisp rolled ginger wafer, often cream-filled, a classic British teatime treat.

clue.text: Hesitated at regular intervals?

definitions.meaning: tottered or wavered, as if unsure
spaced out over time, as working hours or starts are

explanation.definitionFit: Means both tottered unsteadily, as if wavering, and set out in offset spacings, as with staged starting times.

clue.text: Dealing with aspect of philosophy and geopolitics, male getting confused

indicators.note: a jumble of these words means their letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A man muddles global politics with a branch of philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the theory of knowledge, the philosophical study of how and what we can know.

clue.text: Enormous beating

definitions.meaning: as in a ... great majority: very large
a heavy hitting, a pounding with fists

explanation.definitionFit: One word is both an informal intensifier for something huge and the noun or participle for repeated heavy blows.

clue.text: Shed in south-coast location overlooking lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece overlooking another stands above it

parts.note: Hove is a town on the Sussex coast next to Brighton

explanation.surface: A hut in a seaside town has a view of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Hove is a seaside town in Sussex, on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a squalid little hut or shack is a rough shed.

clue.text: Bird rather amusing or unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bird is described as rather funny or strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a slender grey or brown bird of prey, the rarest harrier breeding in Britain.

clue.text: A princess once set up house in a place designated 'gem'

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means lifted from bottom to top, so these letters read backwards

parts.note: Di, the late Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A former princess established a home somewhere nicknamed for jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: The US state of the Rockies is officially nicknamed the Gem State for its mineral deposits.

clue.text: Butter? Gosh — that's hard inside!

indicators.note: the abbreviation is placed within the exclamation

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh
H is short for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a pat of butter is unexpectedly firm.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: this is a particular kind of butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: clarified butter used in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: A bit unhappy, opposing worker with time to collar one is in a relatively weak position

indicators.note: to collar is to grab round the neck, so the long chain of pieces holds the numeral within it

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
sad means unhappy
V, short for versus, means against or opposing
the ant is the crossword's standard worker
an age is a period of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone feeling glum and fighting a colleague over a deadline finds they are on the back foot.
explanation.walkthrough: The collared I sits just after the opening four letters, between the bit and the unhappy part.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to be handicapped or placed less favourably than rivals in a contest.

clue.text: Current area in the mountains specified for woolly animals

indicators.note: these letters are placed inside the mountain range

parts.note: the Alps, Europe's great range
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: An electricity zone in the hills is marked for fleecy livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: South American relatives of the llama kept for their fine fleece.

clue.text: Figure in an old-fashioned way to enjoy computers etc.

parts.words: in an old-fashioned way to enjoy
parts.note: to dig something is dated slang for liking it
IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

explanation.surface: Someone describes a retro fondness for computing in quaint slang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig it' was the 1960s way of saying you liked something.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: each of the numerals nought to nine is a single numeric character, a figure.

clue.text: Spotted former President at party going inside

parts.note: James K. Polk was the 11th US President

indicators.note: the party word is placed within the little word at

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Someone saw an ex-President slipping into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as seen; here it is the adjective for a dotted pattern.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fabric with a pattern of evenly spaced round dots is spotted.

clue.text: Woman of insight giving support to the fellow, a tragic female

parts.note: a prop is a support
he refers to a man
Tess of the d'Urbervilles, Hardy's tragic heroine

explanation.surface: A wise woman backs a man and a doomed heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess is the heroine of Thomas Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles, whose life ends in tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A female seer or oracle is credited with foresight, a woman who foretells events.

clue.text: A section is cut from this crimson material

indicators.note: only a piece of the following words is taken, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A dressmaker trims a length off a bolt of red cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the join of 'this crimson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a loosely woven cotton or linen fabric used for theatre gauzes, lining and cleaning cloths.

clue.text: One could dress Tom Cruise

indicators.note: to dress is also to arrange, as soldiers dress ranks, so the actor's name is set in a new order

explanation.surface: A wardrobe person on a film set might clothe the Hollywood star.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the anagram of the star's name is the very person who might clothe him.
explanation.definitionFit: A costume-maker or supplier provides outfits for actors, so such a person could clothe a film star.

clue.text: Modern baddies set up to achieve celebrity status

indicators.note: in a down entry set up means lifted, so the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: rats are treacherous people

explanation.surface: Contemporary villains are arranged to become famous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the state of being a famous star, celebrity.

clue.text: Frightened, this person had hidden, it's suggested

indicators.note: hidden here means put out of sight, so these letters disappear from the longer word

parts.note: intimidated means frightened
the setter's I had becomes I'd

explanation.surface: A scared person had gone into hiding, according to hints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' is not a hidden-word signal here: it removes I'D. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: hinted at or implied indirectly rather than stated.

clue.text: A landau is travelling around part of Spain

indicators.note: moving about suggests the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A horse-drawn carriage is touring a Spanish region.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the southernmost autonomous region of Spain, home to Seville, Granada and Córdoba.

clue.text: Agitated ambassador, a male beast

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A diplomat is rattled, called a brute of a man.
explanation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency, abbreviated HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: someone worked up and anxious is said to be in a state, flustered.

clue.text: Quixote's not young, keeping fashionable, it's thought

indicators.note: keeping means holding something inside, so the fashion word sits within

parts.note: Quixote is the setter, who says of himself I'm aged
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: The setter admits his age while trying to stay trendy, or so people believe.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym stands for 'I' or 'me': Quixote's not young gives I'M AGED. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something pictured in the mind or supposed was conceived as a belief.

clue.text: Number upset after dinner maybe without a fruit

indicators.note: after means the number part follows the meal part
without means lacking, so the letter goes

parts.note: dinner is an example of a meal

indicators.note: in a down entry upset means turned upside down, so the abbreviation reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone's stomach is upset after eating dinner without fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large sweet fleshy fruit of the gourd family, such as a cantaloupe.

clue.text: Suitable position of hospital in French city

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the city

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: Someone finds a good place at a hospital in the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a comfortable or suitable role or place, as in finding one's niche.

clue.text: Sheep that is seen in shrub

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A sheep has been spotted tangled up in a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Asian nettle-family plant grown for its strong fibre, used in textiles.

clue.text: A country once seen as deficient in its larger setting

indicators.note: deficient means lacking something, here its last letter

parts.note: Siam is the old name for Thailand

explanation.surface: A former nation is seen as falling short within its wider region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'its' refers back to Siam: the larger setting of the old country is the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam, now Thailand, lies in this continent, its geographical surroundings.

clue.text: Group of MPs, including conservative, come and settle time for reform

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in the abbreviation within them
reform means re-form, giving these letters a new shape

explanation.surface: Parliamentarians, Tories among them, are urged to fix a date to change the system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for reform' signals the anagram and 'including' tucks the C in; the surface comma makes 'including conservative' look like a description of the MPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a parliamentary panel of Members chosen to scrutinise a government department or issue.

clue.text: Woman among the top people, 50, was first to be set aside

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
U stands for upper class
L is the Roman numeral 50
led means was in front

explanation.surface: A woman of fifty, mixing with the elite, was once ahead but has been sidelined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' for upper class comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' usage debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a ruling or marriage declared void is cancelled, made legally invalid.

clue.text: Good academician taking some French classes

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician
des is French for some

explanation.surface: A worthy Royal Academy painter signs up for French lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A Royal Academician, a member of London's Royal Academy of Arts, is written RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: ranks or categories by level or quality, as in school years in America.
